name: list-flags
description: Search and browse feature flags in a project. Returns a paginated list scoped to a single environment. Use query to search by name/key, tags to filter by tag, state to filter by lifecycle state (active, inactive, new, launched, archived), and type to filter by temporary or permanent.

query.description: Search by flag name or key

name: get-flag
description: Get detailed configuration for a single feature flag scoped to a specific environment. Returns the full targeting tree including rules, individual targets, fallthrough, prerequisites, and variation details.

name: create-flag
description: Create a new feature flag in a project. Defaults to a boolean temporary flag. After creation the flag is OFF in all environments: use toggle-flag to enable it. For multivariate flags, provide variations array with {value, name} entries.

temporary.description: Whether the flag is temporary (default: true)

name: update-flag-settings
description: Update a flag's top-level settings: name, description, tags, temporary/permanent status, or maintainer. Does NOT modify targeting, rollouts, or rules: use the targeting tools for those. Supported instruction kinds: updateName, updateDescription, addTags, removeTags, markTemporary, markPermanent, updateMaintainerMember.

name: toggle-flag
description: Turn a feature flag's targeting on or off in a specific environment. Returns the previous and new state.

on.description: Whether to turn targeting on or off

name: list-ai-configs
description: Search and browse configs in a project. Returns a paginated list with key, name, mode (agent or completion), tags, and variation count. Use query to search by name or key.

name: get-ai-config
description: Get detailed configuration for a single config including all its variations. Each variation includes its model, instructions or messages, parameters, and attached tools.

name: create-ai-config
description: Create a new config in a project. This creates the config shell: use create-ai-config-variation next to add a model, prompts, and parameters. Mode determines whether variations use 'instructions' (agent) or 'messages' (completion).

mode.description: Agent uses instructions; completion uses messages

name: update-ai-config
description: Update a config's metadata: name, description, tags, or archive status. Does NOT modify variations: use update-ai-config-variation for model, prompt, or parameter changes. Set archived: true to archive (reversible).

archived.description: Set true to archive, false to unarchive

name: delete-ai-config
description: Permanently delete a config. THIS IS IRREVERSIBLE. Requires confirm=true to execute. Prefer archiving (update-ai-config with archived: true) when possible.

confirm.description: Must be true to execute deletion

name: setup-ai-config
description: Create a config with its first variation in one step. This is the recommended way to set up a new config: it creates the config, adds a variation with model and prompts, and verifies everything is configured correctly. Returns the full config detail with variation. To attach agent tools, pass the 'tools' array with {key, version} entries. Use create-ai-config + create-ai-config-variation separately only when you need more control.

mode.description: Agent uses instructions; completion uses messages

name: get-ai-config-health
description: Health check for a config. Detects common issues: missing models (NO MODEL in UI), missing prompts, orphaned tool references, and empty configs with no variations. Returns a health verdict (healthy, warning, unhealthy) with specific issues and per-variation summaries. Run before updating or experimenting with a config.

name: create-ai-config-variation
description: Create a variation for a config. A variation defines the model, prompts, parameters, and tools. modelConfigKey must be in Provider.model-id format (e.g. OpenAI.gpt-4o, Anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5) for models to display correctly in the UI. Agent-mode configs use 'instructions' (a string); completion-mode configs use 'messages' (an array of {role, content} objects). To attach agent tools, pass the 'tools' array with {key, version} entries (create tools first with create-ai-tool).

name: update-ai-config-variation
description: Update a config variation's model, instructions/messages, parameters, or attached tools. All fields are optional: only provided fields are updated. To attach tools, pass the 'tools' array with {key, version} entries (create tools first with create-ai-tool). Pass an empty tools array to detach all tools.

name: delete-ai-config-variation
description: Permanently delete a config variation. THIS IS IRREVERSIBLE. Requires confirm=true to execute.

confirm.description: Must be true to execute deletion

name: clone-ai-config-variation
description: Clone an existing config variation with selective overrides. Reads the source variation, applies any provided overrides (model, instructions, messages, parameters, tools), and creates a new variation. Returns both the source and created variation so you can compare the diff. Use this for A/B experimentation: change one thing at a time while keeping everything else constant.

sourceVariationKey.description: Key of the variation to clone from

name: list-ai-tools
description: List agent tool definitions in a project. Returns each tool's key, description, and schema. Tools are attached to config variations to give models function-calling capabilities.

name: get-ai-tool
description: Get a single agent tool definition including its full schema. Use to inspect a tool's parameters before attaching it to a config variation.

name: create-ai-tool
description: Create a new agent tool definition in a project. The schema should be a raw JSON Schema object with type, properties, and required fields (e.g. {"type": "object", "properties": {...}}). Do NOT use the OpenAI function calling wrapper format. After creation, attach the tool to a variation using update-ai-config-variation.

description.description: Tool description (LLM uses this to decide when to call it)

schema.description: Raw JSON Schema with type, properties, and required

name: get-environments
description: List all environments for a project. Returns each environment's key, name, color, and the credentials that the SDKs need: SDK key (server-side), client-side ID (browser/edge), and mobile key. Use this as the single source for all key types when wiring up an SDK during onboarding -- do not make separate per-key requests.

name: list-feature-flags
description: List feature flags in a project, scoped to a single environment. Returns each flag's key, name, kind, tags, and whether targeting is on. Pagination via limit/offset.

name: get-feature-flag
description: Get detailed configuration for a single feature flag in a specific environment. Returns the full targeting tree: rules, individual targets, fallthrough, prerequisites, and variation details.

name: create-feature-flag
description: Create a new feature flag in a project. Defaults to a boolean temporary flag. After creation the flag is OFF in every environment: use update-feature-flag with {on: true} to turn it on. Use kebab-case keys.

temporary.description: Whether the flag is temporary (default: true)

name: update-feature-flag
description: Update or toggle a feature flag in a specific environment. Pass {on: true} or {on: false} to flip targeting; pass `instructions` (semantic patch instructions) for richer changes (rules, fallthrough, etc.). Returns the previous and new state.

on.description: Whether to turn targeting on or off

instructions.description: Semantic patch instructions for richer changes

comment.description: Optional comment for the audit log

name: get-project
description: Get a project by key. Returns the project's key, name, and environments.

name: recommend-flag
description: Record an ADVISORY recommendation on whether a code change should be placed behind a LaunchDarkly feature flag. This tool is READ-ONLY: it does not create, modify, toggle, or delete any flag. Call it exactly once, as the final step, after you have understood the change and explored the surrounding code. The recommendation is what CI parses to post a pull-request check.

recommend.description: true if the change should be released behind a feature flag, false if it should not

verdict.description: The finer-grained outcome. suggested = a new flag is warranted (pairs with recommend: true). reuse-existing = the change should be gated behind an EXISTING flag that already covers this same unreleased feature rather than a new one — set reuse_flag_key (pairs with recommend: true). already-flagged = the change is already protected by a flag in the diff or an off/mid-rollout ancestor gate (recommend: false). not-suited = there is genuinely nothing to flag: pure refactor, docs, tests, dependency bump, or build/CI/tooling change (recommend: false).

reuse_flag_key.description: Set ONLY when verdict is reuse-existing: the key of the existing flag to gate this change behind (the flag that already covers this feature). Omit for every other verdict.

confidence.description: Confidence in the recommendation, calibrated to how clear the signal is and how much surrounding code you verified

risk.description: Optional. Blast radius / severity of the change itself, independent of confidence. low = small additive isolated change; medium = modified business logic / moderate blast radius; high = cross-cutting, API-contract, data-migration, or auth/payments/data-integrity change.

reasons.description: Concise, evidence-based justifications. Each should cite the specific file, symbol, or behavior that drove the verdict.

name: match-release-policies
description: Preview which release policy governs a flag in an environment and what a policy-based release would do. Before the flag exists pass flagTags for client-side matching; after it exists pass flagKey for the authoritative server-resolved policy. Returns winningPolicy, winningReleaseMethod (immediate|progressive|guarded|null), and any auto-attached metric/metric-group keys.

environmentKey.description: Environment to resolve the policy for

flagKey.description: The flag key (after the flag exists)

flagTags.description: Proposed flag tags (before the flag exists)

name: list-release-policies
description: List every release policy in a project: scope (environments, flag tags), rank, release method, and the guardrail metrics it auto-attaches. Use match-release-policies to resolve which one wins for a given flag + environment; use this only for a full inventory.

name: create-automated-rollout-config
description: Record an automated rollout config that ties a flag to a PR's merge and releases it per environment. Each environments entry is { environmentKey, releaseType }: 'simple' serves true on merge; 'policy' waits until merge and then performs the environment's release policy (immediate/progressive/guarded). Both release that environment on merge. This tool has NO field for holding, scheduling, or a future/notBefore date — to hold an environment, omit it from the environments array entirely (do not add a holdUntil/notBefore/hold field; unknown fields are rejected). Provide the PR reference (repoFullName + prNumber, or prUrl). The guarding flag must already exist.

flagKey.description: The guarding flag key (must already exist)

releaseType.description: simple = serve true on merge; policy = on merge, run the env's release policy (immediate/progressive/guarded). Both release the env on merge; neither holds it. To hold an env, omit it from this array.
